note: Tuesday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Mon 27 Jul US close. The dominant shift held and extended: the US-Iran strike pause reached a THIRD straight night and the oil premium collapsed — Brent -8.7% to ~$88.36, WTI -7.5% to ~$82.61 — which unwound the rate-hike fear and let silver rebound (+2.3% to ~$59.4, first up day/week/month/year since May), gold firm (~$4,098) and crypto catch a bid (ETH +4.4%). US equities mixed at records (S&P +0.02% to 7,413, Dow +0.51% on the oil retreat, Nasdaq -0.18% on NVDA -5% and SanDisk -11%). The FOMC decides Wed 29 Jul; CME hike odds cooled to ~1-in-3 (~33%). 6 of 12 items are dated Mon 27 Jul (last 24h). Every item source-verified; the MAS S-REIT leverage item remains flagged as reported-but-pending primary confirmation.

items.headline: Oil collapses ~9% as US-Iran strike pause holds a third night; Brent back to ~$88
items.summary: Brent crude fell 8.7% to ~$88.36 and US WTI dropped 7.5% to ~$82.61 on Monday as the US and Iran held off attacks for a third straight night, with Washington giving diplomacy 'space'. The move sharply reversed last week's >9% spike (Brent had hit ~$102). Iran denied a reported 10-day ceasefire, and the Houthi/Red Sea front remains a residual risk, so the truce is fragile — but the direct US-Iran de-escalation removed the acute Strait-of-Hormuz supply premium.
items.actionable: This is the upside catalyst the rate-sensitive book was waiting on, now confirmed: the oil collapse unwinds the inflation/rate-hike fear that pressured levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech and crypto — net risk-relief for the largest part of the portfolio (bearish only the small energy long). Watch whether the pause holds into the 29 Jul FOMC; a breakdown re-spikes oil/gold and hardens the Fed's hawkish tilt.

items.headline: Silver rebounds ~2.3% to ~$59.4 — first up day/week/month/year since May; gold ~$4,098
items.summary: Silver spot climbed ~2.3% to ~$59.43 on Monday (September futures opened ~$59.81, +1.5% from Friday), rising over the past day, week, month and year for the first time since May as the weekend Iran pause drove oil sharply lower and loosened the inflation vise that had pinned bullion. Gold rose ~0.7% to ~$4,098, still short of its ~$4,130 two-week high. The metals rebound directly tracks the eased rate-hike fear.
items.actionable: The levered silver core is the portfolio's biggest short-term swing factor and it snapped back hard once the oil-driven rate-hike fear eased — the cleanest expression of the de-escalation relief, since silver is 2-3x more rate-sensitive than gold. Structural deficit thesis intact (JPMorgan ~$81 avg); the 29 Jul FOMC is the next binary — hedge the silver-vs-gold spread into the print rather than adding leverage on the bounce.

items.headline: FOMC decides Wed 29 Jul: hawkish-hold base case, hike odds cool to ~1-in-3 as oil retreats
items.summary: The Fed (chaired by Kevin Warsh since May 2026) is widely expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, with the decision Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET and no SEP. The oil pullback cut CME hike odds back to ~1-in-3 (~33%) from a ~38-40% peak last Thursday, while September hike odds hold near 80%. Warsh has been hawkish in rhetoric — telling Congress the FOMC has 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation' — but offered no firm guidance. Q2 GDP and PCE also land this week.
items.actionable: A live ~1-in-3 hike is still the core near-term threat to levered silver and SGX REITs, but the oil collapse has taken the edge off — the big USD cash pile (earning ~3.5-3.75%) stays productive dry powder for a post-FOMC shakeout. Let the 29 Jul print resolve before redeploying into rate-sensitive names; a dovish Warsh surprise is the upside catalyst, a hawkish hold or hike the downside.

items.headline: S&P and Dow eke out record closes on oil retreat; Nasdaq slips as Nvidia falls 5%, SanDisk -11%
items.summary: US stocks drifted to a mixed close: the S&P 500 added just 0.02% to a record 7,413.18, the Dow gained 0.51% (262.83 pts) to 52,210.08 on the oil retreat, but the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.18% to 24,932.08, weighed by a ~5% drop in AI-chip leader Nvidia. SanDisk plunged ~11% on memory-pricing weakness, keeping the AI-capex/semis unwind alive even as lower oil lifted cyclicals and eased inflation worries into the Fed.
items.actionable: The oil-down/rates-easier tape helped the cyclical and rate-sensitive names the book cares about (Dow, financials, and by extension S-REITs/metals) while the AI-capex unwind (NVDA -5%, memory weakness) is a continuing headwind for the chip leg of the HK-tech core (SMIC). Favor the internet/consumer HK names (Tencent, Xiaomi) over pure-semi exposure; the semis wobble is a US-led read-through into Asia's open.

items.headline: Crypto catches the risk-relief bid: Bitcoin holds ~$65k, Ether jumps ~4.4% ahead of the Fed
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $64,800-65,300 on Monday (up ~1.3% on the day) and Ether jumped ~4.4% to roughly $1,950 as the Iran-pause oil collapse eased the rate-hike fear that had pressured risk assets the prior week. Crypto steadied ahead of the 29 Jul FOMC after last week's ~$225M single-day spot-BTC-ETF outflow. The market continues to trade as a pure risk-appetite barometer off the macro rate channel rather than on any crypto-specific catalyst.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto moves in lockstep with the silver/REIT rate-sensitivity trade — the same Iran-pause relief that lifted silver lifted crypto, hence Ether's outperformance. Treat it as a barometer of the risk-relief impulse; the EU's new offshore-crypto sanctions remain a structural overhang keeping crypto exposure modest versus the metals core.

items.headline: US-Iran hostilities paused a third night to give peace talks 'space'; Iran denies 10-day ceasefire
items.summary: The US and Iran held off attacks for a third straight night, helping lift global stock and bond markets and push oil lower. President Trump, who last week threatened to intensify strikes, is instead giving diplomacy 'some space' per US envoy Mike Waltz; work resumed on restarting negotiations to end the war that began in late February. Tehran denied media reports it had agreed to a 10-day ceasefire, underscoring the fragility of the pause.
items.actionable: The de-escalation is the single biggest cross-book swing and it is holding — a durable pause keeps oil down and rate-hike fear at bay, the tailwind for levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech and crypto. The residual risk is the pause breaking down (Iran's ceasefire denial, the Houthi/Red Sea front) re-spiking oil and gold; keep gold-heavy GDX as the hedge against that tail.

items.headline: AI-overcapacity scare hammers semis: NVDA -5%, SanDisk -11% as memory/AI-capex doubt persists
items.summary: The AI-capex-peak narrative that hit Asian chips (SMIC -10%) last Friday continued into Monday's US session, with Nvidia falling ~5% and SanDisk plunging ~11% on memory-pricing weakness — dragging the Nasdaq lower even as the broad tape held records. Reports that Meta may pivot from proprietary AI models toward leasing spare compute fed fears that AI-infrastructure investment has peaked and overcapacity looms.
items.actionable: A continuing, portfolio-specific headwind for the chip leg of the HK-tech core (SMIC) — but the sharp intra-sector divergence (Alibaba/Xiaomi up, chips down) argues for favoring the internet/consumer names (Tencent, Xiaomi) over pure-semi exposure. Watch whether the AI-capex-peak narrative deepens or fades; it is the main risk against the otherwise-supportive China-stimulus backdrop.

items.headline: China's 24 Jul Politburo signals stronger-than-expected H2 stimulus; anti-'involution' pricing-law draft
items.summary: The Politburo, chaired by Xi, met on H2 economic work and issued stronger-than-expected wording — pledging countercyclical policy 'with precision and force.' The same day the NDRC and market regulator released a draft amendment to China's pricing law (its first update since 1998) targeting 'disorderly low-price competition' (anti-involution). The signalling lands after Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3%, the weakest in three-plus years. China's central bank also injected the most MLF liquidity in five months.
items.actionable: The binary the book was waiting on resolved to the upside — the Politburo's forceful language and the anti-involution pricing reform support the HK-tech core (Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi) into earnings, reinforced by the largest MLF liquidity injection in five months. The Friday/Monday chip divergence argues for favoring Tencent/Xiaomi over the semi leg. Watch for follow-through detail at the Aug policy meetings before adding.

items.headline: Singapore banks at record highs as earnings open; DBS guides FY2026 profit slightly lower
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB hit fresh record highs in July (DBS above S$70) on wealth-management fee income cushioning lower rates, ahead of DBS's 6 Aug results. SGX reporting season opened 23 Jul after hours — Mapletree Industrial Trust posted a DPU of 3.11 cents (-4.9% y/y), and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug. DBS has guided FY2026 net profit slightly below 2025 while reaffirming its 15-cent/quarter capital-return dividend.
items.actionable: SGX banks ride record highs into 6 Aug DBS earnings — supportive for the blue-chip sleeve, but record valuations meet softening guidance and REIT DPUs (Mapletree Industrial -4.9%) already reflect the rate drag. With the Iran pause easing rates, the REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT) should get relief; watch the yield backdrop and the end-July MAS review.

items.headline: MAS reported to be imposing a single S-REIT leverage limit and added disclosures (pending confirmation)
items.summary: Singapore market coverage reports MAS is moving to a single aggregate-leverage limit and additional disclosure requirements for all SGX-listed REITs. The exact effective date and the numeric gearing cap were not confirmable from secondary sources this run and should be verified against the MAS primary release before acting. It would directly touch the portfolio's S-REIT sleeve.
items.actionable: A single leverage cap is a double-edged change for the S-REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT, CapLand China Trust) — clearer rules and more disclosure vs a potential constraint on gearing/acquisitions. Flagged as reported-but-unconfirmed: confirm the cap and date on the MAS site before repositioning the REIT sleeve.

items.headline: Trump EO bars defense contractors from adversary-sourced critical materials — rare-earth reshoring tailwind
items.summary: Trump signed an executive order (20 Jul) further barring US defense contractors from sourcing critical materials from adversaries and directing the Pentagon to mitigate supply-chain national-security risks. It reinforces the structural US rare-earth reshoring push that already includes the DoD's ~15% MP Materials stake, a $110/kg NdPr price floor and a 10-year magnet offtake, plus ~$1.2bn of OSC loans (Energy Fuels, Phoenix Tailings) in June.
items.actionable: Another layer of Western government demand under the ex-China rare-earth watchlist — bullish MP and government-backed UUUU most directly. But with China's export controls suspended to 10 Nov (magnet exports +75% MoM), near-term pricing urgency is eased: accumulate on weakness into the control-snap-back catalyst rather than chase.

items.headline: Houthi blockade forces Saudi crude tankers to U-turn; Saudi Arabia strikes Houthis in Yemen
items.summary: At least seven Saudi crude tankers reversed course toward Suez after the Houthis warned shipowners against calling at Saudi ports; the broader 2026 Hormuz/Red Sea crisis has damaged ~17 merchant ships. Saudi Arabia said it launched strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen after another Saudi vessel was attacked, widening the conflict beyond the direct US-Iran axis and adding a second front to the shipping/energy disruption.
items.actionable: The Red Sea/Yemen front is the residual escalation risk even with the direct US-Iran strikes paused a third night — it keeps a floor under oil and a bid under gold if the maritime disruption widens again. Reinforces gold-heavy GDX and the small energy sleeve as a hedge against the Iran pause breaking down.
